findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp.hail.so" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_sms, list_sms, get_email, list_emails, get_email_raw, get_email_attachment, get_email_events, get_email_stats, get_verification_requirements, check_verification_documents, get_verification, list_contacts, list_email_domains · Private data: upload_email_attachment, create_file_upload, get_call, get_sms, get_email, list_agents, create_agent, route_number, acquire_number, get_number, get_verification_requirements, check_verification, check_verification_documents, submit_verification, get_verification, get_sms_application, amend_sms_application, list_contacts, lookup_contact, whoami, create_contact · Public sink: send_email, upload_email_attachment, create_file_upload, send_sms, get_sms, list_sms, get_email, list_emails, get_email_raw, get_email_attachment, get_email_events, get_email_stats, create_agent, route_email_domain, get_verification_requirements, check_verification, submit_verification, list_verifications, get_verification, get_sms_application, preview_sms_application, amend_sms_application, cancel_verification, confirm_verification, list_contacts, lookup_contact, list_email_domains, whoami, create_contact · Destructive: check_verification, delete_agent.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
